dispersed nano-scale particles were detected in the ACH alloy matrix (Fig. 10 a). The results of high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM, Fig. 10 b) and fast Fourier transform (FFT, Fig. 10 c) revealed that these nano-scale particles were f.c.c Cr particles that maintained a cubic-on-cubic orientation relationship (OR) with the Cu matrix.
A great number of coarse precipitates were detected on ACH alloy matrix due to the slow solidification rate of the alloy during solidification.

Precipitation, fine grain, and dislocation strengthening played important roles in Cu-Cr-Nb alloy
The existence of grain boundaries played a dominant role in strengthening.
With the increase of dislocation density, the ability to resist plastic deformation of the alloy was improved.
in addition to dislocation slip, grain boundary slip and torsion occurred at high temperature.
